1. What shipped (Tracks B/E/F/G, the audit, the 8-bug remediation)
2. The exact 8 bugs fixed, with commit SHAs
3. The root cause writeup — why this happened, pointing at the "found code needs same rigor" memory
4. What's still open — the 4 named test-coverage gaps as the concrete next step, the 41 unverified findings as backlog, and the explicit calibration note ("this does not mean entirety of happy path/corner cases is covered")
5. Where everything lives (memory index, specs, plans, the audit artifact URL)
6. A ready-to-paste starter prompt for the fresh session

Also updated .claude/plans/ACTIVE.md (was stale — still said Track B/E in progress) to reflect Track G shipping and the audit/remediation, with a pointer to the handoff doc.

Not yet committed to git — want me to commit the handoff doc + ACTIVE.md update now, or wait until just ci confirms green first?

Read .claude/plans/SESSION_HANDOFF.md and the memory index at
~/.claude/projects/-Users-gabe-Projects-callisto/memory/MEMORY.md before doing anything else.

Confirm `just ci` is currently green on main — it was still running when the handoff was written,
so don't assume. If it's not green, fix whatever's red before anything else.

Then close the four test-coverage gaps in SESSION_HANDOFF.md §4 (npm::round_trip,
parse_publish_target/release_trigger, probe_git wiring, pre_cursor) one at a time via strict TDD —
red test first, confirmed failing, minimal fix or deletion, confirmed passing, independent
read-only review per fix (explicitly tell every reviewer agent it is read-only and must not run
git stash/checkout/reset/clean), commit. Don't batch them.

After that, tell me what you'd recommend for the remaining 41 unverified medium/low audit findings
(full list at the artifact URL in the handoff doc) rather than starting on them without asking —
that's a scope/priority call I want to make, not one to assume.

6	
7	---

32	
33	**8-bug remediation** — every CONFIRMED critical/high finding from the audit fixed via strict TDD
34	(red test reproducing the exact reported failure scenario → confirmed failing → minimal fix →
35	confirmed passing → independent read-only review → commit). One review-found gap (a fix that had
36	correct logic but an untested branch) was closed rather than accepted. See §2 for the list.

38	## 2. The 8 bugs fixed this session (all committed, all reviewed, all on `main`)
39	
40	1. `bca04b1` — `cargo_publish`'s pre-publish version guard couldn't parse `version.workspace = true`
41	   (the pattern all 10 of this repo's own crates use). Would have hard-failed `callisto publish` on
42	   this repo today. **This bug had ZERO test coverage when it shipped — see §3.**
43	2. `a700bba` — `PublishTarget::NuGet`/`GitHubRelease` silently no-opped the real publish while the
44	   release-tag gate still fired, claiming success with nothing published. Now an exhaustive match +
45	   ecosystem-mismatch validation at walk time (E119).
46	3. `2bb6ca4` + `c09c5f7` — arbitrary file write via unvalidated `changelog` path in `callisto.toml`,
47	   plus `changesets.dir`'s traversal guard missing the absolute-path case. Both now route through
48	   `callisto_model::path::workspace_relative`.
49	4. `bb194cc` — npm's manifest-controlled `publishConfig.registry` field was unvalidated and could
50	   redirect `npm publish`/`npm view` to an attacker host with `NPM_TOKEN` live in the environment.
51	   Now validated against the operator's `[registries]` allowlist (E120).
52	5. `6e16212` + `6b09e48` — subprocess timeout only killed the direct child, not descendants holding
53	   stdout/stderr pipes open, so `PUBLISH_TIMEOUT_SECS` could be defeated forever. Fixed with a
54	   bounded reader-thread grace period (channel-based, no `unsafe`, no process-group/libc calls —
55	   `unsafe_code = "forbid"` is a hard workspace invariant). Both the timeout-kill branch and the
56	   normal-exit branch are now independently tested.
57	6. `d353e54` — Cargo `round_trip` over-corrected a prior bound-crossing fix, bailing on ALL compound
58	   ranges with an upper bound instead of just ones the target actually crosses. The regression test
59	   that shipped alongside the original bug was named `..._is_rewritten` but asserted `is_none()` —
60	   the test documented the bug instead of catching it.
61	7. `def6862` — `[[package-set]]` ecosystem-prefixed glob patterns (`"cargo:pkg-*"`) matched zero
62	   packages, silently, because matching only ever checked the bare name. Independently rediscovered
63	   by 3 of the 8 audit dimension-finders from different angles. `GraphError::PackageSetMatchedNothing`
64	   existed as a safety net but was never constructed anywhere — now a real `DiagnosticCode` fires.
65	
66	Final `just ci` after all 8 fixes: **confirmed green** (all 7 phases — fmt-check, lint, test, audit,
67	doc-check, wasm-check, coverage — exit 0, verified clean, not just exit-code-trusted) on `def6862`,
68	run 2026-08-12. If you're picking this up later and other commits have landed since `def6862`,
69	re-run `just ci` rather than trusting this note.
70	
71	## 3. Root cause of the regressions, and the process fix

74	the working tree at session start (`e0cc091` "publish pipeline hardening", `60e0bef` "package-set

77	
78	**Why:** that batch was committed after checking only "does it compile, does clippy pass, do the
79	*existing* tests pass" — never run through canon→vector→lambda, never given a fresh adversarial
80	pass, never TDD'd. One of the bugs (`bca04b1`'s version-check) shipped with **zero test coverage at
81	all**, not even a happy-path test.
82	
83	**This is now a saved lesson** — read it before treating any future "found in the working tree"

96	Keep doing that explicitly in every reviewer prompt going forward.
97	
98	## 4. What's still open — the recommended next step
99	
100	Four test-coverage gaps the audit named explicitly, NOT yet touched by the remediation pass. These
101	are concrete, already-scoped, and cheap — either wire the code up with real tests or delete it if
102	it's genuinely dead:
103	
104	1. **`npm::round_trip`** (`crates/callisto-manifests/src/npm.rs:395-411`) — zero test coverage
105	   anywhere; its only reachable path (`preserve_npm_ranges = true`) is never set `true` in any test.
106	   Also rejects npm's idiomatic space-separated compound ranges (`>=1.0.0 <2.0.0`) with no test
107	   documenting this as intentional.
108	2. **`parse_publish_target`/`parse_release_trigger`** (`crates/callisto-graph/src/config/resolve.rs:148-163`)
109	   — only `"none"`/`"crates-io"` are ever parsed by any test; `"npm"`, `"pypi"`, `"nuget"`,
110	   `"github-release"`, and the invalid-string error path are untested despite being from this

112	   the exact current shape before writing tests.)
113	3. **`probe_git`/`check_git_version`** (`crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/git.rs:1-13`) — built to
114	   give a friendly `IncompatibleVersion` diagnostic for git < 2.20, but never called anywhere outside
115	   its own definition and has no test. Wire it into `load_workspace` before any git-dependent
116	   operation, or remove it if it's not wanted.
117	4. **`pre_cursor` tracking** (`crates/callisto-conventional/src/pre_cursor.rs:1-57`) — zero test
118	   coverage, and the field it would populate (`TagIndex.pre_cursor`) is hardcoded empty everywhere
119	   downstream. Looks like a half-wired, abandoned feature — wire it up with tests or remove the dead
120	   exports; don't leave it half-built.

11	Do not distribute publish-pipeline fixes across parallel agents, even when they appear to touch different files.
12	
13	**Why:** Semantic coupling runs through shared traits (CommandRunner, RegistryClient), shared data flow (plan → load_plan → execute → publish), and activation dependencies (fixes that make previously-dead code live simultaneously). Parallel agents each see a slice and cannot reason about secondary effects in other agents' slices. A fix that looks correct in isolation can be a no-op or actively wrong given what another agent changed.
14	
15	**How to apply:** Fix the publish pipeline sequentially, one phase at a time, with full CI after each phase. Parallel agents are appropriate for *reading/investigation* (each agent reads a different slice, findings merge cleanly) but not for *writing* in semantically coupled systems.
16	
17	**Parallel investigation vs parallel fixing:** The 5-investigator audit workflow found 38 bugs effectively. That was parallel reading — correct use. The prior fix workflow (w08vr56yl) had one agent correctly fix Bug1 (publish order) while the order fix was a no-op because ManifestRole::Platform was never assigned — something a different agent was supposed to fix but in a way neither agent coordinated. Semantic coupling, not file overlap, is the constraint.

commit e0cc091821d8aea1aaad22848c8ab66e0dcf41f6
Author: Gabe Castro <gabe@techworx.dev>
Date:   Wed Aug 12 11:41:10 2026 +0200

    feat(publish): package filter, registry resolution, subprocess hardening
    
    Squashes several tightly cross-referential publish-pipeline changes that
    would not build standalone if split further:
    
    - plan_publish/publish gain a --package filter (errors on unknown names
      rather than emitting an empty plan) and convert previously-fatal git/
      changeset/tag lookup failures into soft Diagnostics.
    - npm publishConfig.access/registry is now read from package.json and
      respected over the scoped-package --access public default; fixes
      publishing to a private registry with publishConfig.access: "restricted".
    - SubprocessRegistryClient (publish_client.rs) now runs each publisher
      from the package's own directory instead of the workspace root, guards
      against publishing a version that doesn't match the plan, runs
      `python -m build` before `twine upload` (twine had no dist/ artifacts
      on a clean checkout), adds npm --registry / pnpm --no-git-checks / bun
      lockfile support, fixes PEP 427 wheel-filename normalization (dots
      weren't collapsed, only hyphens), fixes a false-positive rate-limit
      match on cargo's "429.1KiB compressed" summary line, and extends
      already-published detection to npm/twine E409 and mixed skip+upload
      output.
    - Publish orchestration caps rate-limit retries (MAX_RATE_LIMIT_RETRIES)
      so a 429 loop can no longer hang forever, adds a progress callback so
      `callisto publish` prints per-package status, and treats is_published()
      errors as non-fatal (falls through to attempt publish rather than
      aborting on a flaky pre-check).
    - CommandRunner gains run_with_timeout (default delegates to run(), so
      existing mock runners are unaffected); CliCommandRunner implements it
      with spawn+poll+kill and background-thread stderr streaming to avoid
      pipe deadlock. Used for the 300s publish subprocess timeout.
      New CommandError::TimedOut (E025).
    - PublishAttemptResult::Failed now carries a machine-readable `kind`
      (serialized as errorKind: rateLimited/authFailed/network/other) derived
      from RegistryError::kind_str(), so callers can distinguish failure
      types without parsing the message string. Wired through the text
      renderer and JSON report output.
    - RegistryKey gains PYPI/NUGET well-known constants, consumed by
      PublishTarget::{Pypi,NuGet}::registry_key().

input.description: Read-only review of probe_git removal decision
input.prompt:
STRICTLY READ-ONLY REVIEW — you must not run `git stash`, `git checkout`, `git reset`, `git clean`, or any command that mutates the working tree or git state. Only read files and run non-mutating commands (cargo build/test/clippy are fine; git status/diff/log are fine).

Repo: /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto (Rust workspace, `unsafe_code = "forbid"` everywhere).

Context: This is closing a named test-coverage gap: "`probe_git`/`check_git_version` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/git.rs:1-13`) — built to give a friendly `IncompatibleVersion` diagnostic for git < 2.20, but never called anywhere outside its own definition and has no test. Wire it into `load_workspace` before any git-dependent operation, or remove it if it's not wanted." This is uncommitted in the working tree — do not commit it, just review it. Run `git diff` and `git status` yourself to see the actual change (it's a deletion: `git show --stat` won't work since it's uncommitted, use `git diff --stat` and `git diff`).

Unlike the other two gaps closed earlier this session (which added tests, and one of which fixed a real bug), THIS gap was resolved by **deleting** the dead function rather than wiring it in. What changed:
1. Deleted `crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/git.rs` entirely (was exactly 13 lines: just the `probe_git<R: CommandRunner>(runner: &R, cwd: &Path) -> Result<(), CommandError>` function, which shells `git --version` and calls `callisto_model::check_git_version` on the output).
2. Removed `pub mod git;` and `pub use git::probe_git;` from `crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/mod.rs`.
3. Left `callisto_model::check_git_version` (in `crates/callisto-model/src/exec.rs:94-122`) and its existing test (`parses_git_version`, exec.rs:128-133) completely untouched — that function already had test coverage and is not part of what was deleted.

**The reasoning behind choosing deletion over wiring** (please adversarially challenge this, not just confirm it):
- Grepped every `git` CLI invocation in `crates/callisto-vcs/src/shell.rs` and `access.rs` (the actual subprocess call sites for the shell-fallback git backend) and found no flag/feature that specifically requires git >= 2.20 — `rev-parse HEAD`, `tag --list`, `log --format=...`, `tag <name> <sha>` are all long-supported. So the `>=2.20` floor doesn't appear to gate any actually-used capability; it reads as an arbitrary "require something reasonably modern" floor picked at initial authorship, never connected to anything.
- There is no single existing call site that all git access flows through: `changed.rs`, `tags.rs` (via `TagIndex::build`), `aggregate.rs` (two places), `infer.rs`, `commands/tag.rs` in callisto-graph, plus `callisto-conventional/src/window.rs`, ALL independently call `callisto_vcs::GitAccess::discover(root, runner)` directly — there is no single funnel point in `callisto-graph` (e.g. `Workspace::load`) that all of these pass through, so wiring `probe_git` into `Workspace::load` would NOT actually guard most of these call sites, and would run even for commands that never touch git at all (violating the codebase's own documented lazy-cost philosophy, e.g. see the doc comment on `Workspace.tags: OnceCell<TagIndex>` in `crates/callisto-graph/src/lib.rs` explaining why `TagIndex` is built lazily rather than eagerly in `Workspace::load`).
- `callisto_vcs::GitAccess::discover(root, runner) -> Self` (in `crates/callisto-vcs/src/access.rs`) is the actual shared dispatch point all those call sites go through, and its doc comment explicitly states "Never fails" and it returns `Self`, not `Result<Self, _>`. Wiring a fallible version-probe in there would require either (a) breaking that infallibility contract and changing the signature across 8+ call sites (a genuinely separate, larger task), or (b) adding new memoized/lazy-check state inside `ShellGit` (in `crates/callisto-vcs/src/shell.rs`) fired on first actual shell invocation, which would require touching every one of `ShellGit`'s ~6 methods and updating its ~15 existing unit tests' mock `CommandRunner`s to also handle a `["--version"]` call — real design work, not a mechanical "wire it in."
- Found a direct precedent already in this exact codebase for the same situation: `crates/callisto-moon/src/extension.rs:16-33`'s `check_moon_version` is ALSO a version-check utility with zero production callers (only referenced by its own test), and it carries an explicit doc comment explaining why it's deliberately left unwired ("moon negotiates plugin/host version compatibility out of band... This helper is therefore kept as a standalone, independently-tested utility rather than being wired into `register_extension`"). `check_git_version` already has equivalent test coverage; `probe_git` (the now-deleted wrapper) did not, and unlike `check_git_version`, `probe_git` had no independent value as a "standalone utility" — it was purely a thin CommandRunner-shelling adapter with nothing to keep.
- `CommandError::IncompatibleVersion` (the error variant `check_git_version` returns) and `REQUIRED_GIT` were deliberately left untouched rather than also removed, since `CommandError` is `#[non_exhaustive]` public API in the foundational `callisto-model` crate, and removing a public enum variant is a larger, separate API-surface decision out of scope for closing this one coverage gap.

Please adversarially review:
1. **Is deletion actually the right call, or should this have been wired in?** Specifically: is there a call site or wiring point I missed that WOULD be a clean, small, non-breaking way to connect `probe_git` (or a re-added equivalent) into the real call graph? Look especially hard at whether `Workspace::load` or `GitAccess::discover` could reasonably be made to do this cheaply without the breaking-change concerns described above — don't just accept my reasoning, try to falsify it.
2. **Verify the "no version-gated flag" claim independently** — check `crates/callisto-vcs/src/shell.rs` and `access.rs` yourself for any git invocation that might actually depend on a modern-git-only behavior (e.g. certain `--format` placeholders, `rev-parse` flags, or default-branch-name assumptions) that would make the >=2.20 floor load-bearing after all.
3. **Verify `check_moon_version` really is an accurate precedent** — read `crates/callisto-moon/src/extension.rs` yourself and confirm the parallel holds.
4. **Confirm no breakage**: run `cargo build --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo test -p callisto-graph` and `cargo clippy -p callisto-graph --all-targets -- -D warnings` yourself (don't trust reported numbers) to confirm nothing else in the workspace referenced `probe_git`, `locate::git`, or the deleted module, and that removal is clean.
5. **Scope check**: confirm `crates/callisto-model/src/exec.rs` (`check_git_version`, `CommandError::IncompatibleVersion`, `REQUIRED_GIT`) was genuinely left untouched (`git diff` should show zero changes to that file).

Report status (concerns / no concerns), and if you believe wiring-in was actually the correct choice over deletion, say so explicitly with your reasoning and a concrete proposed wiring point — I want a genuine second opinion on this judgment call, not just a rubber stamp.

input.description: Read the design rationale for pre_cursor in section 8

result.output:
already-specified rules rather than adding a new one: §7.5's new-member exemption
(force-set to the group's current target version, no divergence error) applies exactly as
in normal mode, and at that same moment an `initialVersions` entry is synthesized for the
new member equal to the group's *current* `initialVersions` entry — giving it a proper
pre-release baseline retroactively rather than leaving it absent from `pre.json`. §7.5's
drift cross-check firing every run for the duration of the pre-release cycle until resolved
is expected behavior, consistent with how every other warn-by-default cross-check in this
spec works — no pre-mode-specific suppression.

**`ReleaseTrigger::Auto` packages in pre-mode** cannot be tracked via `pre.changesets`
(byte-compatible with `@changesets/cli`, which has no conventional-commits concept, so
`pre.json`'s schema has no field for "commits already counted" — and P1 forbids adding one).
This needs a marker distinct from §9.1's release tags — a release tag means "this got
published" (P2's stateless signal), which `version` never creates (§9.1, §13 invariant 24,
no exception). A pre-mode commit-boundary marker means something else entirely ("inference
already counted commits up to here"), so it's a **separate git ref namespace**, not a tag:
`refs/callisto/pre-cursor/<PackageId>` — written by `version` itself at the moment it
computes a pre-mode bump for an `Auto`-trigger package, alongside the manifest write (same
mutation phase, §7.6), and included in the calling workflow's existing `git push --tags`
step (§9.3) by pushing `refs/callisto/pre-cursor/*` alongside real tags — no new push step,
just a wider ref-spec on the one that already exists. Because it lives outside `refs/tags/`,
it can never collide with or be mistaken for a real release tag, so it doesn't need §9.1's
"only after success" rule at all — it's bookkeeping about *what inference already saw*, not
a signal about *what got published*. The next run's commit-based inference for that package
scans commits since this cursor ref, not since its last *stable* release tag — so
already-counted commits are naturally excluded without any new
`pre.json` field, and repeated `version` invocations in pre-mode are correctly idempotent
for `Auto`-trigger packages, the same way they already are for `Changeset`-trigger ones.

`callisto snapshot --tag <tag>` computes a transient, non-persistent version (e.g.
`0.0.0-snapshot-<sha>`) and writes it to manifests **uncommitted, untagged** — it never
creates a tag and never publishes (§9's coordinator posture applies here identically; an
earlier draft described `snapshot` as a "publish path," which was a leftover from the
pre-§9 orchestrator design and has been corrected). `snapshot`'s `--format json` output
carries the computed version and affected packages, not a `published`/`publishedPackages`
pair — actually publishing the snapshot manifests is the calling workflow's job, exactly
like every other publish in this design (§9.3's pattern). `snapshot` and pre-mode
(`pre.json` present with `mode: "pre"`) are mutually exclusive — invoking `snapshot` while
in pre-mode is a hard error, since both compute a version by a different, incompatible rule
from the same on-disk state.

The reviewer noted a correct fix needed to swap in `GitAccess::discover(...).head_sha()` while PRESERVING the hard-fail-on-total-failure contract (there's a spec invariant, docs/01-spec.md §G.11 "SPEC DECISION, pinned invariant #33", and an existing test `test_snapshot_sha_resolution_failure_is_surfaced_error` requiring `plan_snapshot` to return `Err(GraphError::Vcs(_))` when HEAD cannot be resolved at all — not silently substitute a fake sha).

This is uncommitted in the working tree — do not commit it, review only. What changed in snapshot.rs:
```rust
// before:
let repo = callisto_vcs::GitRepository::discover(&ws.root)?;
let sha = repo.head_sha()?;
// after:
let sha = callisto_vcs::GitAccess::discover(&ws.root, ws.runner).head_sha()?;
```
Plus `use callisto_vcs::GitDataSource;` added to bring the trait method into scope.

What changed in snapshot_tests.rs: a new test, `test_snapshot_resolves_head_sha_via_command_runner_fallback_when_gix_unavailable`, using a tempdir with no real `.git` (asserted via `callisto_vcs::GitRepository::discover(...).is_err()`) and a hand-rolled `FakeHeadShaRunner` that routes `git tag --list` (needed because `TagIndex::build` runs first, using the same runner) to an empty tag list and `git rev-parse HEAD` to a canned 40-char sha, then asserts `plan_snapshot` now SUCCEEDS (previously this exact scenario — no gix-discoverable repo, but a runner able to answer `rev-parse HEAD` — would have hard-failed regardless of what the runner returned, since the old direct `GitRepository::discover` call never consulted `CommandRunner` at all). Also a doc-comment fix on the pre-existing `run_git` helper (was stale, claiming HEAD resolution "talks to a real on-disk repo directly" — no longer true).

2. **Is the new test doing what it claims?** Verify `FakeHeadShaRunner` genuinely can't succeed via native gix (the tempdir really isn't a git repo) and that the 40-character sha it returns is a plausible/valid `CommitSha` per `crates/callisto-model/src/identity.rs`'s `CommitSha::parse`.
3. **Scope discipline**: is swapping `GitRepository::discover` for `GitAccess::discover(...).head_sha()` here fully equivalent in every OTHER respect (not just the fallback behavior) — e.g. does `GitAccess`'s native-gix path behave identically to a direct `GitRepository::discover` when a real repo IS discoverable (same error types, same success semantics)? 4. Run `cargo build --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo clippy -p callisto-graph --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo fmt -p callisto-graph -- --check` yourself.
